findings.title: OffsetTracker can commit past an offset gap after the prior offset is committed
findings.body: In get_committable_offsets, start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset) treats every offset below min_offset as already accounted for. If a gap exists before min_offset, it is forgotten after the first commit because mark_committed removes all offsets <= the committed offset from all_offsets. For example, with completed offsets 100, 102, and 103, the first call commits 100 and removes it; the next call sees min_offset=102 and last_committed=100, so start=102, and it returns 103, committing past missing offset 101. This violates the class's gap-handling contract and can cause Kafka offsets to be skipped if such a gap ever occurs.

findings.title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure
findings.body: Each work_queue is created as queue.Queue() with no maxsize. Since submit never blocks, a slow group or worker can accumulate an unbounded number of queued WorkItems and offset-tracking entries. The class docstring claims 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but these queues never fill. Under sustained slowdown this can exhaust memory and take down the consumer instead of slowing Kafka consumption.

findings.title: Shutdown exits workers before queued items are drained
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown = True while work is still queued, then calls q.shutdown(immediate=False) and joins. OrderedQueueWorker.run checks self.shutdown at the top of its loop, so a worker that is between items exits immediately without draining queued WorkItems. A worker blocked on get() may also not be woken by Queue.shutdown(immediate=False), causing join(timeout=5.0) to return while the daemon thread remains blocked. The result is queued messages not processed on shutdown and leaked worker threads; those offsets will be reprocessed after restart, causing duplicate work.
